Title: Stand up a Samoa high-value monitoring lane
Finding: All 14 high-value tickets (>$5,000) in April routed to Samoa, and 64% of them landed in Legal Hold. The pattern is a corridor-concentration risk: high-ticket-value × single-destination × single-disposition.
Impact: Compliance exposure (potential AML/structuring), customer wait time on the highest-value transactions, and reputational risk if Legal-Hold backlog grows.
Recommendation: Create a dedicated Samoa high-value queue with mandatory pre-send EDD for selling > $5k and a named compliance partner SLA on Legal-Hold release.

Title: Reduce EW103 inbound-call dependency with proactive comms
Finding: EW103 alone accounts for 215 of 357 tickets (60%). It's the single largest source of inbound calls into the APAC desk.
Impact: Concentrated handle-time cost; every minute shaved off EW103-related calls cascades. Also a single-point-of-failure risk for digital sending volume.
Recommendation: Ship proactive status SMS/email for Sent-to-Corresp and Posted statuses for EW103 senders; add an in-app order-status check before offering the call-us CTA.

Title: Close the repeat-contact loop on stalled orders
Finding: 65 distinct orders generated repeat tickets in April; the worst — order AU1157296364 — was called about 7 times. Repeat-contact friction signals customers are not getting closure on first interaction.
Impact: Doubles handle-cost per resolved order; erodes customer trust on already-stressful issues.
Recommendation: Add a 'previously contacted' flag on the agent screen so the second-touch agent inherits context; set a 48h proactive-callback on Legal-Hold and To-Cancel orders.

Title: Investigate APAC Care long-tail handling
Finding: 62 tickets exceeded 24-hour resolution; 47 of them sat with Ria - APAC Care. Mean resolution (1,669 min) is two orders of magnitude larger than median (9.2 min).
Impact: Hidden in averages — these are the orders that generate executive escalations.
Recommendation: Run a root-cause review on each >24h ticket; suspect drivers are Modification + Recall workflows that need correspondent ping-pong. Define a 4-hour interim-status SLA so customers aren't left in the dark.

Title: Treat CEC 1002 as the Samoa Legal-Hold signal
Finding: 34% of tickets are CEC-flagged; code 1002 dominates the flagged set and aligns tightly with Legal-Hold disposition on Samoa transactions.
Impact: If 1002 is the de-facto AML/structuring flag, treating it operationally as such would let the floor route faster.
Recommendation: Confirm CEC code semantics with Compliance, then build an auto-route rule: CEC 1002 + Samoa + high-value → straight to APAC Compliance group, skipping the Ria - Care first touch.

Title: Address the Refund + Legal-Hold reason concentration with a workflow refresh
Finding: Refund (78 tickets) and Legal hold (47 tickets) together account for ~40% of all calls — both are post-send friction reasons, not pre-send confusion.
Impact: Customer-experience damage compounds when refund cycles stretch; agents repeat the same explanation across multiple touches.
Recommendation: Draft a one-page customer-facing 'what to expect when your transaction is on hold / being refunded' explainer and embed in the SMS/email proactive comms from rec #2.

Title: Resolve the cross-channel reporting gap (Feb messaging)
Finding: March + April messaging tickets are present in this analysis, but a Feb messaging file was not delivered. Channel-mix conclusions for Feb 2026 are therefore inbound-only.
Impact: Trend-call on messaging adoption (chat / WhatsApp) is two months instead of three — narrow base for any pattern call.
Recommendation: Re-pull the Feb 2026 messaging-tickets APAC export and rerun build_report.py to backfill. This is a 5-minute data ops task.

Title: Negotiate stall-time SLAs with the top correspondent
Finding: 101 tickets (28% of volume) touched Ria Open Payment Network. Its share of stalled (non-terminal) tickets is over-represented vs. its volume share.
Impact: Correspondent stalls are the upstream driver of Legal Hold and Refund tickets — fixing them removes work from the call centre.
Recommendation: Open a payout-partner SLA conversation with the top correspondent on Posted → Paid turnaround time and Legal-Hold release acknowledgement.
